title: Real-time quantum simulation of hadron production in deep inelastic scattering
authors: Xianghui Cao, Meijian Li, Yang Li, Wenyang Qian
abstract: We develop a quantum simulation framework for meson production in deep inelastic scattering based on light-front QCD Hamiltonian formalism. A quark-antiquark dipole, prepared either as a single-momentum state or as the $q\bar q$ component of a virtual photon, is evolved in real time through the color field of a nuclear target via Trotterized unitary evolution. We consider both proton and gold nuclear targets, each characterized by their respective saturation scale. From the evolved state we extract the transverse momentum broadening, the total and elastic cross sections, and the $J/ψ$ production rate by projecting onto the $J/ψ$ light-front wavefunction. We then extract the nuclear modification factor $R_A$ at different photon virtuality $Q^2$ and analyze nuclear modification effect. Results of classical simulations show good agreement with analytical eikonal predictions across a broad range of parameters. For the single-momentum dipole, quantum simulation is demonstrated on a quantum circuit emulator with a smaller lattice size, and results are consistent with the classical benchmark. This work establishes a first-principles, amplitude-level pathway toward computing exclusive hadron production in deep inelastic scattering, directly relevant to the physics program of the Electron-Ion Collider.
summary: This work pioneers a first-principles, amplitude-level quantum simulation approach to model how quarks and gluons evolve into hadrons during Deep Inelastic Scattering. By simulating the dipole propagation through a nuclear color field, the authors calculate key observables like the nuclear modification factor, providing crucial insights for future collider experiments like the Electron-Ion Collider.
main_problem: The paper aims to understand the real-time evolution of quarks and gluons produced in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) as they hadronize within the color field of a nuclear target.
main_result: The quantum simulation framework successfully calculates observables like the nuclear modification factor ($R_A$) and dipole cross sections, showing agreement with eikonal predictions in the classical limit.
method: The primary method is developing and applying a real-time quantum simulation framework based on the light-front QCD Hamiltonian formalism, benchmarked against classical simulations.
model_or_system: The system models the process $\gamma^* + p/A ightarrow J/\psi + X$, where the virtual photon fluctuates into a $q ar{q}$ dipole that propagates through the color field of a nuclear target (Proton or Gold). The dynamics are governed by the light-front QCD Hamiltonian in the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory.
key_observables: Transverse momentum broadening, total and elastic dipole cross sections, $J/\psi$ production rate, and the nuclear modification factor ($R_A$).
important_parameters: Photon virtuality ($Q^2$), target type (Proton, Gold), and the small-$x$ regime characteristic of the CGC theory.
main_assumptions: The simulation uses a discrete momentum basis and initially focuses on the $|q ar{q}angle$ Fock sector, relying on the eikonal approximation for initial benchmarks.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the DIS process ($\gamma^* + p/A ightarrow J/\psi + X$), and the text describes extracting observables by projecting onto the $J/\psi$ light-front wavefunction.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical problem (DIS hadron production), details the theoretical framework (light-front QCD, CGC), describes the simulation methodology (Trotterized unitary evolution on a quantum circuit emulator), and presents calculations for key observables like cross sections and $R_A$.
why_interesting: While the core physics is high-energy QCD, the methodology—using quantum simulation to model non-equilibrium, real-time evolution in a complex many-body background field—is highly relevant to open quantum systems dynamics and quantum field theory simulations.
